title: [a11y] Heading hierarchy has one h1 and no skipped levels
test_data: Expected: 1 h1, then h2 sections, then h3 subsections
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
List all headings (h1-h6) in DOM order with their levels
expected_result: There is exactly one h1, section headings are h2 and sub-headings are h3; no heading level is skipped.

title: [a11y] No heading is empty
test_data: Known empty headings: h1 (page), h3 under "Who We Are"
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
List all headings and read their text content
expected_result: Every heading element has non-empty text (currently the h1 and one h3 under "Who We Are" are empty).

title: [a11y] Content images have non-empty alt text
test_data: Images: Who We Are image, 5 portraits, 2 card images, Environmental Values image
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Scroll slowly from top to bottom so every section is revealed (some sections are hidden until scrolled into view)
Read the alt attribute of each content image
expected_result: Every content image has a non-empty, descriptive alt. Purely decorative images may use alt="" but the 5 portraits are content images.

title: [a11y] Social links have an accessible name with the network
test_data: Links: Instagram, LinkedIn, Facebook, YouTube (currently all named "social profile - opens in a new tab")
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Scroll to the footer
Read the accessible name of each social link (aria-label or image alt)
expected_result: Each social link has a distinct accessible name that includes the network name, for example "Instagram - opens in a new tab".

title: [a11y] All links have a non-empty accessible name
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Collect every a element and compute its accessible name (text, aria-label, or image alt)
expected_result: No link has an empty accessible name (including the logo link and the social links).

title: [a11y] Hamburger can be focused and operated with the keyboard
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Press Tab until the hamburger receives focus
Press Enter
Close it, then repeat with Space
expected_result: The hamburger is reachable with Tab, shows a visible focus indicator, and opens/closes the menu with Enter and Space (currently it is a <span> without tabindex or role).

title: [a11y] Hamburger exposes role, label and expanded state
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Inspect #menu-burger-opener attributes
Open the menu and inspect again
expected_result: The control has an appropriate role (button), an accessible name (aria-label) and aria-expanded that changes between false and true.

title: [a11y] Header navigation follows a logical tab order with visible focus
steps: Open /about/ on the dev environment and wait for the page to finish loading (about 3 seconds, so hero animation completes)
Press Tab repeatedly from the top of the page through the header
Observe focus position and indicator at each stop
expected_result: Focus moves through the logo and nav links left to right, a focus indicator is always visible, and there is no keyboard trap.
